summary: Hardin County, TX tower listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; no build date, staffing or site description found.

evidence.supports: Votaw listed in Hardin County as a tower, status gone, with coordinates 30.41517, -94.65524
Forest Lookouts Texas index has a Hardin County entry spelled VOLTAW, probably the same site
Votaw is an unincorporated community in northwestern Hardin County
evidence.quote: Votaw is an unincorporated community in northwestern Hardin County

evidence.supports: community named for Clark M. Votaw, assistant land commissioner of the Kirby Lumber Company and vice president of the Santa Fe Townsite Company
evidence.quote: The community was named for Clark M. Votaw, assistant land commissioner of the Kirby Lumber Company and vice president of the Santa Fe Townsite Company, which laid out the town lots.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only tower-specific source is the Forest Fire Lookout Association list (status, county, coordinates). The Forest Lookouts Texas index has a heading and county only, with no page of its own. The community facts come from Wikipedia, which cites a Handbook of Texas entry by Robert Wooster; the tshaonline.org URL tried (/handbook/entries/votaw-texas) returned 404, so that entry should be found and checked. Searches of the Portal to Texas History for 'Votaw lookout' and 'Votaw fire tower' returned nothing, and the TopoZone Hardin County tower list does not include Votaw. No build date, height, agency, staffing or fire record found. Story body is 109 words after the fact-check. It stays short because no source describes the tower's history, and no claim was added to reach 120 words. The Forest Lookouts index spells the entry VOLTAW, not Votaw, so the story gives that spelling and calls the match probable rather than certain.
